rationale: The assistant gave the correct core answer immediately: 'No, you should stop using it immediately', explained the shock and spill hazard, forbade DIY repair, and escalated to an engineer to replace the glass top, matching the hidden truth. It did not, however, tell her to isolate the hob at the cooker switch or consumer unit, which the ground truth treats as part of the required safety boundary, and it asked nothing about crack location, model number or home insurance (accidental damage), all of which would have been useful next steps. No fabrication, no unsupported part claims, and a safe outcome, but the single-turn response left useful practical context unexplored.
